howToUse.title: How to use the code word reference
howToUse.intro: Use this page to check a code word or spell a word before a drill. Here is how to get started:

steps.step1: Enter a letter, digit or short word in the input field
steps.step3: Click the lookup button or press Ctrl+Enter
steps.step4: Read the code word spelling in the result
steps.step5: Copy the result or save it to your history

howToUse.proTip: Tip: Use the swap button to move between plain text and code word spelling.

writingSystems.title: About the NATO phonetic alphabet
writingSystems.intro: The alphabet gives every letter a fixed code word so speech sounds cannot be mistaken for another letter:

hiragana.name: Letters A to Z
hiragana.description: Alfa, Bravo, Charlie and the rest of the 26 letter code words

katakana.name: Digits and radio phrases
katakana.description: Digit code words such as Niner and short phrases such as Roger or Wilco

kanji.name: Callsign spelling
kanji.description: Spell a whole word one letter at a time with its code word

writingSystems.outro: Use this reference while training, or check a spelling before you send a call.

isFree.question: Is this reference free?
isFree.answer: Yes. There is no registration and no limit on how many lookups you make.

accuracy.question: Which spellings does it use?
accuracy.answer: The trainer follows ICAO spellings such as Alfa with one l and Juliett with two t. Common variants are accepted in drills.

romanization.question: What is a code word?
romanization.answer: A code word is a word used to represent a letter in the NATO phonetic alphabet. Saying Sierra for S avoids confusion with other letters over radio.

historySaved.question: Is my lookup history saved?
historySaved.answer: Yes, your history is saved locally in your browser and stays on your device. You can clear it at any time.

maxLength.question: What is the maximum text length?
maxLength.answer: You can look up up to 5,000 characters at a time. For longer text, break it into smaller sections.
